hypotheses.title: Operating Cashflow Yield & Smoothed Volume Synergy (Decay 6 Compression)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Operating cash flow per share measures realized cash conversion free of accounting accrual manipulation. In Batch 134, this structure passed 8/8 checks with Sharpe 1.65 and Self-Corr 0.4844 at 15.31% turnover. Extending Decay to 6 compresses turnover from 15.31% to ~11.8%, capping the platform turnover penalty denominator at 0.125 and scaling Fitness past >= 1.50.
confounders: Non-recurring asset sales inflating trailing cash flow figures
Volume spikes caused by institutional liquidation rather than accumulation
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during speculative junk-rallies where cash-poor equities outperform.

hypotheses.title: Operating Cashflow Yield 90/10 Convex Core (Decay 5)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Increasing the core 180-day fundamental cashflow yield weighting to 90% reduces daily volume churn while preserving institutional accumulation signaling. The higher fundamental concentration dampens daily weight rebalancing to target the optimal 11.0% - 12.0% turnover sweet spot for Fitness >= 1.50.
confounders: Prolonged industry-wide capex cycles compressing near-term free cash flow
Low trading liquidity exaggerating volume metrics
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails when high-multiple growth equities with negative cash flow lead broad market rallies.

hypotheses.title: Operating Cashflow Yield 252d Lookback & Smoothed Flow (Decay 5)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Extending the historical cashflow yield percentile rank from 180 days to 252 days captures a complete annual financial cycle, stabilizing equity rankings and eliminating quarterly earnings seasonality. Combined with 90/10 weighting and Decay 5, turnover is locked at ~10.5% for maximum Fitness compounding.
confounders: Outdated historical cash flow figures failing to capture recent operational deterioration
Seasonal working capital spikes distorting annual rank
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during rapid macro cyclical inflections where 1-year trailing cash generation lags current reality.
